Suspect S1: Use of standard equality operator instead of constant-time comparison for password hashes
Category: security
Location: src/werkzeug/security.py lines 146-146 (new version)
Suspected problem: Switching from hmac.compare_digest to a standard == string comparison introduces a timing side-channel vulnerability, allowing attackers to measure comparison time to determine parts of the hash.
What would confirm or refute it: Inspect python security best practices regarding password verification and check whether `_hash_internal(method, salt, password)[0]` and `hashval` are sensitive strings that require constant-time comparison.

evidence.note: Standard equality operator used instead of hmac.compare_digest to compare password hashes.
check_password_hash verifies stored password hashes against newly computed hashes.

arguments.explanation: In `check_password_hash`, comparing password hashes (`_hash_internal(method, salt, password)[0]` and `hashval`) using standard equality (`==`) short-circuits on the first mismatch. This creates a timing side-channel vulnerability where an attacker can measure the time taken to perform comparisons and incrementally recover the valid password hash. `hmac.compare_digest` must be used instead to ensure constant-time comparison.
arguments.claim: Replacing hmac.compare_digest with standard equality comparison == for password hash checking introduces a timing side-channel vulnerability.
